s1.syndrome_frame: Acute respiratory distress with facial and nasal swelling in a patient with uncontrolled diabetes and recent COVID-19 infection
salient_findings: Black eschar on the nasal root
Presence of fungal hyphae and spores in nasal mucosa
key_facts: Patient had COVID-19 infection at the end of December 2022
Patient was admitted to hospital on January 1st, 2023
Patient developed new symptoms on January 11th
Initial examination showed heart rate of 116
Initial examination showed respiratory rate of 26
Initial examination showed blood pressure of 150/88 mmHg
Initial examination showed O2 saturation of 90% in room air

salient_findings: Black eschar on the nasal root
Presence of fungal hyphae and spores in nasal mucosa

Patient was admitted to hospital on January 1st, 2023

shortlist.label: Mucormycosis
shortlist.why_kept: Presence of fungal hyphae and spores in nasal mucosa histological examination, and detection of Rhizopus microsporum and Mucor racemosus in blood metagenomics next-generation sequencing

shortlist.label: Invasive fungal sinusitis
shortlist.why_kept: CT scan of head showing pansinusitis, and presence of fungal hyphae and spores in nasal mucosa histological examination

shortlist.label: Rhizopus infection
shortlist.why_kept: Detection of Rhizopus microsporum in blood metagenomics next-generation sequencing, and presence of fungal hyphae and spores in nasal mucosa histological examination

shortlist.label: Mucorales infection
shortlist.why_kept: Detection of Mucor racemosus in blood metagenomics next-generation sequencing, and presence of fungal hyphae and spores in nasal mucosa histological examination

shortlist.label: Aspergillosis
shortlist.why_kept: Recent COVID-19 infection and uncontrolled diabetes increasing susceptibility to opportunistic fungal infections

raw.rationale: The patient's symptoms, including facial and nasal swelling, black eschar on the nasal root, and pansinusitis, along with the detection of Rhizopus microsporum and Mucor racemosus in blood metagenomics next-generation sequencing (mNGS) and the presence of fungal hyphae and spores in the nasal mucosa histological examination, are consistent with Mucormycosis, a rare but serious fungal infection that often affects individuals with uncontrolled diabetes and those who are immunocompromised.

rejected.label: Invasive fungal sinusitis
rejected.why: While the patient has pansinusitis, the presence of fungal hyphae and spores in the nasal mucosa and the detection of Mucorales in mNGS suggest a more specific diagnosis of Mucormycosis.

rejected.label: Rhizopus infection
rejected.why: Rhizopus is a genus of fungi that can cause Mucormycosis, but it is not a specific diagnosis.

rejected.label: Mucorales infection
rejected.why: Mucorales is an order of fungi that includes the causative agents of Mucormycosis, but it is not a specific diagnosis.

rejected.label: Aspergillosis
rejected.why: There is no evidence in the patient's symptoms, laboratory results, or imaging studies to support a diagnosis of Aspergillosis.
